title: N. parisii infection of C. elegans
author: Emily Troemel

steps_raw.instruction: Note: This protocol has been optimized for infecting L1 stage worms on a 6 cm plate for a maximum of 30 hours. Infections of older stage worms or later timepoints may require different amounts of food to avoid starvation.
1. Pick 20 L4 worms to a 10 cm OP50/NGM plate for each strain to be tested.
2. After 4 days at 20°C, bleach worms and hatch eggs overnight in M9. Take 6 cm unseeded NGM plates out of the cold room so they are at room temperature when setting up infection.

For each 6 cm plate, want 150 ul superfood, 1200 L1 worms, and spores (we have been using 1.5x10^6 spores/6 cm plate) in 500 ul total. If setting up replicates, make one "master mix" of food/spores/worms and split between the plates.

First make up a food + spores mix. Aliquot this into a separate tube for each strain to be tested. Then add worms and M9 if necessary to make up volume, and invert to mix. Add 500 ul of spores/food/worms mix to unseeded 6 cm NGM plate, tilt to spread liquid over entire surface area, and dry in hood.
4. Incubate plates at 25°C after they are dry.
